query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a small amount of Nb into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Nb
generation.conditions: Alloy composition: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy; Processing conditions: Induction melting; Test conditions: Room temperature and high-temperature (up to 700°C) oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable single-phase solid solution with a body-centered cubic (BCC) structure
generation.mechanism: The introduction of Nb can refine the grain size, reduce the formation of intermetallic compounds, and enhance the formation of a stable single-phase solid solution, leading to improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (e.g., strength, ductility), enhanced corrosion resistance, and improved high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy without Nb addition
generation.boundary: Alloy composition: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy; Nb content: 0-5 at.%; Processing conditions: Induction melting; Test conditions: Room temperature and high-temperature (up to 700°C) oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Nb addition and the resulting microstructure and properties of the alloy are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with and without Nb addition, and test their mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with Nb addition does not show improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance compared to the alloy without Nb addition, the hypothesis is falsified
